summary.text: Timothy Murphy is the Democratic candidate for Indiana State Senate District 19 in the November 3, 2026 general election, in which he faces Republican Blake Fiechter for a seat with no incumbent.
A pastor in Fort Wayne running for office for the first time, he listed a stronger safety net and democratic reform among his priorities in a Ballotpedia survey.

paragraphs.text: Timothy Murphy graduated from Lone Oak High School, earned a bachelor's degree from Centre College in 2004, graduated from Eden Theological Seminary in 2007, and earned a Ph.D. from the Claremont School of Theology in 2014, according to Ballotpedia.
His career experience includes working as a pastor.
In a Ballotpedia survey, Murphy said he grew up in Kentucky, has lived in Fort Wayne since 2018, and serves full time as pastor of a local church.
He said this is the first time he has run for office.

His key messages included a strong safety net, with universal child care in every county, paid parental leave, paid sick leave, affordable health care and a living wage, funded through a progressive state income tax.
He listed democratic reform, economic justice, taxes, supporting families and the environment as his policy areas.
